scope_note: Prospective planning input; no contract frozen, no loop executed, no calculation run by this lens. Model family throughout: fixed-spacing SU(2) Kogut-Susskind patterned family on Z^3 (24-link factors, selected triple, 21 omitted anchored face classes with coefficient alpha*tau/24 grouped into whole-star interactions, delta=alpha/8), unless a goal explicitly names a finite graph.

goal_pairs.title: Exact finite-graph sign certificate for the interaction shift, labelled non-AQ (advisor route a)
goal_pairs.model: finite_graph_exact: the 48-link Wilson cover R={0,e_z} of the patterned family (two complete 24-link factors), selected triple (0,0,0), the seven incident whole-star interactions phi_b with omitted coefficient alpha*tau/24, electric Casimirs on every link, representation cutoff j<=j_max with a certified tail, a declared boundary completion (open links vs star-complete), tau frozen on a moderate grid such as {+-1e-3,+-1e-2,+-1e-1} (dimensionless coupling; alpha, hbar, spacing fixed).
goal_pairs.observable: Delta_G(tau)=m_G(tau)=<Omega_G(tau),W Omega_G(tau)> (finite-graph Wilson mean, exactly 0 at tau=0) with certified sign and enclosure; secondarily I_G(tau)-I_G(0) for the finite-graph inverse-energy form; exact rational or interval linear algebra decides.
goal_pairs.control: (i) tau->-tau sign flip: first-order shift must flip, a symmetric response flags an even-order or arithmetic artifact; (ii) j_max->j_max+1 with certified tail: sign persists; (iii) two boundary completions: a completion-dependent sign identifies no bulk effect; (iv) exact Fraction admission with python-flint Arb replay; (v) tau=0 replay returns exactly 0.
goal_pairs.why: Executable now with exact arithmetic and the only route that can show a sign at moderate tau; but it is a different, finite model, so its gate must carry model_class=finite_graph_exact, transfer_status=not_transferred_to_AQ and the sentence 'not an AQ-state result' (rule R8).

goal_pairs.title: tau=0 replay and resolving-power ratio for the AT6 pipeline (reference_unresolved label)
goal_pairs.model: The admitted AT6 zero-selected AQ subfamily pipeline (selected (0,0,0), tau=+1e-14, L=1e9, s in [0,128], 4097 nodes) replayed with tau=0 exactly, and the same budget evaluated prospectively at the cap tau=1e-8.
goal_pairs.observable: rho_j = (certified width at node j) / (prospective first-order shift bound c_1|tau|, with |m|<=D as placeholder until G3 supplies c_1); and the byte-level difference between the tau=0 and tau=1e-14 certified intervals.
goal_pairs.control: If the tau=0 replay reproduces the interacting interval up to the D terms, the pipeline carries no interaction information by construction; rho>1 at every node labels the certificate reference_unresolved; the label and its definition are frozen before the replay.
goal_pairs.why: Cheap, exact, and it makes the Besant-Leadbeater failure mode (agreement with a reference built into the readout) impossible to commit silently; it also fixes the vocabulary the later shift loops need.

goal_pairs.title: First-order Wilson-mean coefficient c_1 with an explicit second-order remainder (advisor route b, derivation half)
goal_pairs.model: Finite-volume full Hamiltonian of the patterned family at selected (0,0,0); AM2 creation expansion e^{-C}Omega_0 with anchored norm ||c||_a<=R=1/64, J<=28|tau|, majorant G(t)=16e^{8t}(1+10t); local observable W on the cover R; passage to the AQ subsequential state via local trace-norm convergence stated as a separate obligation.
goal_pairs.observable: omega_tau^{(V)}(W)=c_1 tau + r_2(tau) with c_1 an exact rational and |r_2(tau)|<=c_2 tau^2 with explicit c_2, uniformly in volume; likewise omega_tau(W^2)-1/4.
goal_pairs.control: Sign flip tau->-tau (c_1 tau changes sign); consistency with G1's finite-graph m_G(tau) at the smallest grid tau (consistency, not proof); normalization <psi,psi> and the annihilation adjoint bounded in the same anchored norm; a failed remainder constant is recorded as insufficient, not as a lower bound.
goal_pairs.why: It is the advisor's own derivation target for both the cap and the shift goals; its falsifiable content is the sign of c_1, which G1 can check on the finite graph.

goal_pairs.title: Cap-level target with a pre-registered sufficiency floor
goal_pairs.model: AQ state at the original cap tau=+1e-8, selected (0,0,0), original centered xz Wilson, one frozen s* (proposal s*=1), L free.
goal_pairs.observable: Certified radius of C_tau(s*) against a frozen absolute target (proposal 2e-6, or a Euclidean-side argument replacing the real-time Duhamel term).
goal_pairs.control: The prospective floor min_L E(s*) ~ 1.2e-6 to 1.3e-6 from HNM-AT6-F06 is written into the contract before evaluation; an outcome above the frozen target is insufficient by construction and is recorded with its dominating term; no tau change inside the loop.
goal_pairs.why: Honest negotiation of the target per advisor observation 2, instead of a second silent coupling change (the AT5 precedent is retained as a model change, not a refinement).

goal_pairs.title: Statement-only dictionary between the two-plaquette hardware SU(2) model and the patterned cover
goal_pairs.model: Kavaki-Lewis two-plaquette Kogut-Susskind SU(2), j in {0,1/2}, x=2/g^4, versus the patterned family's cover R with the AL1 dictionary tau=96/g^4 at uniform coefficients; every parameter classified (coordinate, regulator, coupling, state preparation, measured, model deformation) with units.
goal_pairs.observable: None; a dictionary and a parameter table, plus the statement of which terms the patterned family omits or selects relative to the uniform two-plaquette Hamiltonian.
goal_pairs.control: Consistency of the two dictionaries at uniform coefficients; explicit failure statement if the patterned cover cannot be mapped to a two-plaquette graph.
goal_pairs.why: The only external numbers with stated uncertainties (95% confidence intervals on ibm_lagos) exist for such tiny graphs; the dictionary decides whether they can ever serve as a calibration control for G1. Hardware numbers are never validation of an AQ certificate.

strategy_changes: R1 Freeze before any outcome: model id, observable formula with centering convention, s* or whole grid, five-term error structure (state/boundary, dynamics/cutoff L, truncation j_max, quadrature, arithmetic), target, outcome taxonomy, and claim_exclusions containing 'free reference inside the enclosure implies no interaction claim'; hash all of it in the contract and freeze.json.

R2 Outcome taxonomy retained in gates: accepted_within_scope | limited | insufficient, with sub-labels reference_unresolved (interval contains the matched free value) and sign_certified_finite_graph (non-AQ); every limited/insufficient record names the dominating term and its numerical share.

R3 Insufficient outcomes record the failing term and the smallest change of a frozen parameter that would pass, as a planning note only; a changed parameter is a new loop with a new contract and is named as a model change.
R4 No post-hoc s*: whole grids are reported; no node of maximal separation is chosen afterwards; declared pilot runs at reduced size are excluded from the counted result.

R5 Mandatory discriminating controls for any claimed shift: centering identities with perturbed m_hat and the s=0 endpoint check; two boundary families or completions; monotone j_max and L sequences with certified tails; exact Fraction vs Arb/mpmath.iv replay and -O byte-identical replay; tau=0 null replay; tau->-tau sign flip.

R6 Independence: a claimed shift needs paired producers with unread current work or a single producer with a skeptic replay from the contract alone; shared premises declared; same-author passes never called independent (the AIR shared-judge confound, restated).

R7 Deterministic blinding: the comparison to the reference and the threshold live in the frozen contract and are computed by check.py; producers commit code before the first full-size evaluation (adapted from the muon g-2 lattice freeze-then-unblind practice).

R8 Finite-graph sign certificates carry model_class=finite_graph_exact, explicit graph and completion, j_max, tau, statement with sign and enclosure, transfer_status=not_transferred_to_AQ, claim_exclusions [AQ thermodynamic state, infinite volume, uniform Hamiltonian, continuum], check-id prefix FG-, the gate sentence 'This certificate concerns the finite graph G; it is not an AQ-state result', and a website model badge.

Assessment of advisor observation 3: agreed that O(tau)-error methods are structurally reference-inside; route (b) needs both exact c_1 and an explicit c_2 remainder paid in the anchored norm including normalization and the adjoint, with the AQ passage as a separate obligation; the (+tau,-tau) pair is a built-in control for both routes and should be frozen as such; route (a) is honest only as a labelled finite-graph certificate or as a consistency check on c_1.

skill_updates.proposed_text: Freeze the observable, the readout time and the acceptance threshold before any outcome is seen; report every batch and every insufficient outcome with its dominating error term; a maximum selected among candidates after inspection is not a prior-fixed observable (documented cautionary case: the 1952 astrological experiment in Jung's Synchronicity, pilot batch folded into the total, maxima chosen among fifty aspects, probability recomputed three times).

skill_updates.location: New paragraph after the Clay paragraph
skill_updates.proposed_text: A certificate whose enclosure contains the matched free reference is reference-unresolved; agreement with a reference that is built into the readout is not evidence (documented cautionary case: Besant and Leadbeater's number-weights, defined as count/18 and then 'checked' against the atomic-weight table). Require a null replay of the same pipeline at zero interaction and a resolving-power ratio before any interaction claim.

skill_updates.location: New paragraph after the reference-unresolved paragraph
skill_updates.proposed_text: An exact finite-graph certificate is a statement about that finite graph. It must carry model_class=finite_graph_exact and transfer_status=not_transferred, and its gate must say 'not an AQ-state result' (or the name of the actual target state). Kepler's Harmonices Mundi records where the harmonic idea failed (the periodic times) and labels Fludd's harmonies symbolism rather than mathematics; the modern rule is a label the validator can test.

The 1995 AIR evaluation of remote viewing itself records that the same viewers, judge and targets made independent effects impossible to identify; treat shared premises and correlated authorship in this workbench the same way.

Fetch tools truncate long pages; an archive.org OCR or a long PDF counts as read only when the passage was located in the downloaded raw text, and quotations returned only by a tool summary are not quotations.

tools: python-flint (Arb balls, exact fmpq) and mpmath.iv as independent replays of every exact Fraction certificate; never for admission.

A contract-hash step: check.py refuses to run unless the contract's frozen (model, observable, s*, target, taxonomy) hash matches freeze.json; the reference comparison and threshold are computed inside check.py.
A tau=0 replay wrapper for the AT6 pipeline producing a byte-level interval diff (goal G2).

Optional SDP preview (cvxpy with an open-source solver) for positivity/loop-equation bounds on a finite graph, labelled preview only, as an independent cross-check of an exact linear-algebra sign certificate.
Local source workflow: curl the raw OCR/HTML/PDF, extract text streams in Python, grep the passage; record offsets and page running heads in the ledger.
disagreements: With the framing that route (a) resolves roadmap goal 'shift': a finite-graph sign certificate resolves a shift in a finite model only; the AQ goal stays open unless a comparison bound smaller than |Delta_G| is proved.

With advisor observation 1's optimism about an O(tau) state bound from AM2 without cost: the non-unitary e^{-C}, the normalization and the adjoint each cost weight in the anchored norm, so the first loop on that route should be a derivation statement (G3), not a datum.

With any use of 2024-2026 hardware numbers as comparison targets for the AQ family: none measures a Wilson-loop or plaquette expectation in a 3+1D Kogut-Susskind SU(2) model comparable to ours; two-plaquette numbers are calibration controls at most, after G5.
Ranking: the skeptic may prefer G2 (cheapest, labels first) above G1; this lens ranks G1 first because it is the only executable route to a sign, provided R8 is enforced.
open_questions_for_skeptic: Is the tau->-tau sign-flip control sufficient to exclude an arithmetic artifact at second order, or must the (+tau,-tau) difference itself be certified with a separate error budget?

How should two 'boundary completions' of the 48-link cover be defined so that they are genuinely different models (open links vs star-complete vs embedded in a larger exact graph), and which one is closest to the AQ centered-box state?

Is the tau=0 replay a valid null control given that D=2 sqrt(49|tau|/3) is defined with |tau| (so the tau=0 interval collapses the state term), or should the null control keep D fixed and set only the interaction to zero?
Does a declared reduced-size pilot contaminate the freeze if the same code path is used for the counted run; what must be logged to prove the pilot data were excluded?

What evidence shows that a threshold was fixed before outcomes were seen (git commit ordering, freeze.json timestamps, hash of the contract inside the producer inputs), and is that evidence testable by reproduce.py?
For G3, which anchored-norm bookkeeping of the annihilation adjoint is acceptable, and does the AQ passage require more than local trace-norm convergence for the second-order remainder?
